note.headline: Apple slips to 342.56; still priced above every value estimate as forecasts fall

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business, but at 342.56 the price needs faster growth than Apple is delivering, and analysts keep cutting forecasts.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because resistance sits just above the price and the overall tech market is weak.
summary.act_at: Buy at or below 300.56; add near 266.84

note.happening: Apple fell 1.9% to 342.56. That puts it just under a resistance zone (a price area where selling has stopped rises before) at 342.73–345.08 and below its 20-day average of 347.31. The Verge reported that Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-28.
note.business: Today's news does not change the business. The AI-agent hiring was reported, not announced in a filing. It points to a future product, not to sales or margins today. The Black Friday deals story is only about sentiment. The business itself is doing well. Sales grew 15.06% over the last twelve months to 478.8B. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. Debt is not a risk: Apple has 80.1B of debt against 36.3B of cash, but yearly cash generation covers the gap easily. Two things are at risk. First, growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth fell to 11.72% from 16.6% two quarters ago. Second, inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. Unsold products can force price cuts and lower margins. The newly added investigation risk in the annual report is a governance issue for now. It is not yet a business one.

worth.text: Every valuation method puts Apple below today's price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash, discounted at 10.1% a year) gives 142.56 in the bear case, 197.73 in the base case and 258.87 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history (share price compared with sales per share) gives 222.1 to 300.56. At 342.56, the price assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 26.5% a year. Apple's sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years. The multiples tell the same story. Apple trades at 38.1 times last year's earnings and 32.3 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio is 10.4, against a peer median of 5.2, and it sits at the 98th percentile of its own five-year history. The methods differ mainly on the starting growth rate. At 20% growth the value is 266.84, and at 30% it is 390.22. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 199.72.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price needs about 26.5% a year, while sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, so the business produces a lot of spare cash.
Operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%, so Apple keeps more profit from each dollar of sales.
The share count fell 1.56% in a year, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice of the profits.
bear: The price-to-sales ratio of 10.4 is double the peer median of 5.2 and at the 98th percentile of Apple's own five-year history.
Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, which could force discounts and lower margins.
Analysts have cut next-quarter EPS (earnings per share) to 2.15 from 2.24 a month ago, a 3.8% drop, and quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.72% from 16.6%.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 197.73–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of my range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history. It is close to the rising 200-day average of 302.79. Buying starts to make sense at or below this level.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still faster than last year's 15% sales growth. Adding makes sense here.

longterm.why: The business is high quality, but the price assumes growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price is moving sideways. It sits just under resistance at 342.73–345.08, with more at 347.89–351.46, and its typical daily move (ATR, average true range) is 8.17. That leaves little room to gain, and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 351.46, or on a pullback that holds the 335.96–338.44 support zone.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.7% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.6% move by 2027-02-19, a window that includes the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: The price falls to 300.56 or lower, near the 200-day average of 302.79. That would be a buy.
The 2027-01-28 report shows quarterly sales growth back at 16.6% or higher with operating margin at or above 33.01%. That would raise my range.
The next-year EPS estimate climbs back above 10.84, where it stood 30 days ago, instead of drifting down from 10.6.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The price fell to 342.56 but stays above the 300.56 top of the value range, and the next-quarter EPS estimate was cut 3.8% in 30 days.
